metadata.title: Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study (TIMSS) 2023: National report for England Volume 2

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This TIMSS 2023 national report for England Volume 2 uses TIMSS assessment results for year 5 and year 9 mathematics and science, together with TIMSS questionnaires completed by pupils, teachers, and headteachers, and (for some pupil characteristics) linked National Pupil Database (NPD) information. The report describes that analyses are based on the achieved samples and that response rates were considered for some questionnaire-based sections (e.g., teacher questionnaire response thresholds for inclusion in exhibits). However, the provided text does not specify whether complex survey weights (e.g., student sampling weights) or replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were applied, nor does it name any weight variables. Because the report is primarily descriptive/associational (comparisons of means/percentages and benchmark attainment) rather than an ML modeling pipeline, the manuscript does not document a weight application strategy in the excerpt; analysts should consult the TIMSS 2023 methodology documentation for the international database to apply the appropriate complex-sample weights when reproducing estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report’s excerpt does not document how missing data were handled for the questionnaire-derived variables and linked NPD characteristics, nor does it describe any explicit missing-data procedure (e.g., listwise/pairwise deletion or imputation). This is a reporting gap for reproducibility because TIMSS questionnaire and linkage datasets typically contain nonresponse and missingness, and the report includes many subgroup comparisons and associations that would be sensitive to the missing-data strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report analyzes TIMSS 2023 year 5 and year 9 mathematics and science performance for England, and it includes subgroup analyses using pupil characteristics available from the National Pupil Database (NPD) (not all pupils could be matched, e.g., pupils in the independent school sector are excluded from NPD-linked analyses). For questionnaire-based sections, the report states that teacher questionnaire response rates were taken into account and that findings were included only if based on data for more than 50% of pupils (within the IEA international exhibit thresholds). For some international comparisons, the report notes exclusions due to non-participation in questionnaires/assessments (e.g., Canada year 9 not participating in assessments and New Zealand year 9 minimum participation not satisfied; Singapore pupils not participating in some questionnaires; and Finland/France/Lithuania year 9 questionnaire exclusions for specific items). Beyond these documented restrictions, the excerpt does not provide a full list of item-level or case-level inclusion/exclusion rules.

data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS 2023 National Report for England Volume 2 synthesizes England’s year 5 and year 9 mathematics and science performance using TIMSS achievement scores and international benchmarks, and it links these outcomes to a wide set of pupil, teacher, school, and home-environment questionnaire measures. The report reports many statistically significant associations (e.g., boys outperform girls in year 5 and year 9 mathematics; FSM eligibility and fewer books at home are associated with lower achievement and lower benchmark attainment; and pupil confidence, instructional clarity, and school climate factors are associated with higher performance), but it explicitly cautions that these are associations rather than causal effects. It also documents changes over time (notably gender gaps re-emerging in 2023 compared with 2019, and increased absenteeism categories). The excerpt does not provide ML model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/R²) because the analysis is not presented as an ML predictive pipeline; therefore, no ML techniques are extracted. Limitations include reliance on self-reported questionnaire data, NPD linkage exclusions (e.g., independent school sector), and incomplete reporting in the excerpt on missing-data and weighting procedures.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an IEA/OECD-style national report that primarily presents descriptive and associational results (means, benchmark attainment percentages, and questionnaire-based associations) rather than training/evaluating machine learning models. Consequently, there are no ML algorithms, no ML target-variable prediction pipeline, and no ML performance metrics to extract. The excerpt also does not report the final analytic sample size (total N) or per-country N, so sample size fields remain null despite the report being empirical.
